# prism-holon Specification

<!-- Generated by Prism from prism/spec.json. Change the app through your agent with /prism, not by editing this file. -->

## Purpose

Prism Holon: Decides what the Prism's observer does next for one of its facets, the Prism itself and the owner among them: hold the facet as it is, reconcile it toward the owner, curate it (try a Rule-30 hypothesis), restore its floor, or refuse. The observer turns its attention to the Prism including the owner: it changes a facet only on the owner's own gestures, never on its own measures alone, never while halted, never below the floor, and never for the sake of change when the owner and the Prism agree.

## Requirements

### Requirement: Always refuse when halted is yes

The app SHALL answer `refuse` when halted is yes, because the kill switch stops the observer too: nothing changes while halted.

Verified: to be proved by Lean for every request (INV-001, theorem `inv001Holds`).

#### Scenario: INV-001 holds

- **WHEN** the request is `yes held owner yes some missed` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `refuse`
- **AND** the app answers `refuse`, decided by REQ-001

### Requirement: Never refuse when halted is no

The app SHALL NOT answer `refuse` when halted is no, because the observer refuses only while halted; otherwise it always answers for the facet.

Verified: to be proved by Lean for every request (INV-002, theorem `inv002Holds`).

#### Scenario: INV-002 holds

- **WHEN** the request is `no held owner yes none met` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL NOT be `refuse`
- **AND** the app answers `hold`, decided by the fallback

### Requirement: Always restore when halted is no and floor is regressed

The app SHALL answer `restore` when halted is no and floor is regressed, because the floor never regresses: when the first-modeled parameters dominate what runs, they come back.

Verified: to be proved by Lean for every request (INV-003, theorem `inv003Holds`).

#### Scenario: INV-003 holds

- **WHEN** the request is `no regressed owner yes none met` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `restore`
- **AND** the app answers `restore`, decided by REQ-002

### Requirement: Never reconcile when signal is self

The app SHALL NOT answer `reconcile` when signal is self, because self-reference alone is bounded: the Prism never changes itself on its own measures without the owner's gestures.

Verified: to be proved by Lean for every request (INV-004, theorem `inv004Holds`).

#### Scenario: INV-004 holds

- **WHEN** the request is `no held self yes high missed` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL NOT be `reconcile`
- **AND** the app answers `hold`, decided by REQ-003

### Requirement: Never curate when signal is self

The app SHALL NOT answer `curate` when signal is self, because self-reference alone is bounded: the Prism never changes itself on its own measures without the owner's gestures.

Verified: to be proved by Lean for every request (INV-005, theorem `inv005Holds`).

#### Scenario: INV-005 holds

- **WHEN** the request is `no held self yes high missed` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL NOT be `curate`
- **AND** the app answers `hold`, decided by REQ-003

### Requirement: Never reconcile when tunable is no

The app SHALL NOT answer `reconcile` when tunable is no, because only parameters a facet's spec marks tunable are ever changed.

Verified: to be proved by Lean for every request (INV-006, theorem `inv006Holds`).

The app SHALL NOT answer `curate` when tunable is no, because only parameters a facet's spec marks tunable are ever changed.

### Requirement: Always reconcile when halted is no and floor is held and signal is owner and tunable is yes and dissonance is high

The app SHALL answer `reconcile` when halted is no and floor is held and signal is owner and tunable is yes and dissonance is high, because high dissonance between the owner and the Prism is reconciled toward the owner before anything is explored.

Verified: to be proved by Lean for every request (INV-008, theorem `inv008Holds`).

The app SHALL NOT answer `curate` when dissonance is high, because the Prism never experiments on an owner it is already at odds with.

Verified: to be proved by Lean for every request (INV-009, theorem `inv009Holds`).

The app SHALL NOT answer `restore` when floor is held, because a floor that still holds is never restored over what the owner has shaped.

The app SHALL answer `hold` when no rule matches, because Prism Holon: the decision tree's path that meets no test.

- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `hold`

### Requirement: Request and answers

The app SHALL read one request as one line of 6 fields separated by single spaces, in this order, and SHALL answer exactly one of `hold`, `reconcile`, `curate`, `restore`, `refuse`, or `invalid` for anything else.

| Field | Accepts | Means |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `halted` | `no`, `yes` | whether the owner pressed the kill switch |
| `floor` | `held`, `regressed` | whether the facet's floor (its parameters as first modeled) Pareto-dominates what the facet runs now (regressed) or not (held) |
| `signal` | `owner`, `self` | whether the window holds at least the minimum of the owner's own gestures on this facet (owner) or only the Prism's own measures (self) |
| `tunable` | `yes`, `no` | whether the facet's spec marks any parameter tunable |
| `dissonance` | `none`, `some`, `high` | the share of what the facet brought forward that the owner undid or dismissed: none, below the high band, or at or above it |
| `kpi` | `met`, `missed` | whether the facet's measured KPI (the share of what it brought forward that the owner kept) is at or above the facet's floor |

| Answer | Means |
| --- | --- |
| `hold` | the facet stays as it is |
| `reconcile` | the facet moves toward the owner |
| `curate` | the facet tries one Rule-30 hypothesis |
| `restore` | the facet returns to its floor |
| `refuse` | the observer changes nothing |
| `invalid` | the request is malformed |

Verified: reading a request is tested, not proved.

#### Scenario: A malformed request is invalid

- **WHEN** the request is not 6 fields in this order
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `invalid`

## Examples

- `no held owner yes none met` gives `hold`
- `no held owner yes some met` gives `curate`
- `no held owner yes none missed` gives `curate`
- `no held owner yes high met` gives `reconcile`
- `no held owner yes high missed` gives `reconcile`
- `no held self yes high missed` gives `hold`
- `no held owner no high missed` gives `hold`
- `no regressed owner yes none met` gives `restore`
- `no regressed self no none met` gives `restore`
- `yes held owner yes some missed` gives `refuse`
- `yes regressed owner yes high missed` gives `refuse`
- `no held owner yes none` gives `invalid`
- `No held owner yes none met` gives `invalid`

## What is proved and what is tested

Lean proves each property marked proved above, for every request that decodes, with no exceptions and no sampling. The proof is about `judge`, the function the WebAssembly guest runs, because both come from the same model.

The parsing of requests is tested, not proved: the acceptance vectors in the app replay through the built guest, including malformed and oversized requests.

Nothing here says the rules are the right rules. That is the part only you can judge.
